Hallbar Consulting Inc. and Research Institute of Sweden (RISE) (2017). Resource Supply Potential for Renewable Natural Gas in B.C. Public Version, March 2017. Prepared for the Province of British Columbia (Electricity and Alternative Energy Division, BC Ministry of Energy and Mines), FortisBC Inc. and Pacific Northern Gas Ltd. No report number or DOI printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 1; the cover is unnumbered). A resource-potential study: the public version prints NO technology costs (no capex, opex or levelized cost for digesters, landfill-gas upgraders or gasification), so the to-get needed-for (Canadian AD and bio-SNG plant costs) is not met. Loaded the few technology-level numbers: assumed operating capacity of AD plants (80%) and of landfill-gas upgrading (~95%), descriptions and state of wood-to-RNG technology, and methane yields per tonne of feedstock (complete-mix AD and gasification/pyrolysis) as flows per t feedstock as received (per-unit t = t feedstock, not per GJ product; WWTP sludge is per t BOD). Yields are feedstock properties under study assumptions, mostly from Swedish sources (RISE, Varmeforsk 2012, JTI 1988). Other-values: $28/GJ price assumption, provincial potentials, landfill capture 75%. Not loaded: Tables 2-6 (WWTP, pulp mill, landfill and forestry feedstock inventories) and figure values.
